subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-class delayed agent-turn contract, and if so should the initial product scope be cron-only or shared across cron, sessions, subagents, and heartbeat?
rationale: The current stream contract cannot safely express multi-hour provider jobs, and choosing persistence, tool-loop, fallback, delivery, and public config semantics is a product/API decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Design shared delayed turns
options.body: Introduce a provider-neutral delayed-turn lifecycle and initially wire cron, with other background surfaces adopting the same contract afterward.

options.title: Narrow to cron only
options.body: Specify an intentionally cron-scoped batch contract first, accepting later migration work if sessions and heartbeat need a broader abstraction.

options.title: Do not add batch routing
options.body: Keep synchronous agent turns as the product contract and direct users to external batch pipelines for stateless workloads.

recommendation.title: Design shared delayed turns
recommendation.body: Introduce a provider-neutral delayed-turn lifecycle and initially wire cron, with other background surfaces adopting the same contract afterward.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review and feature history connect this person most directly to the cross-cutting provider, cron, and runtime contract decision.
